title: Simple His-Tag Column Prep Procedure
author: Dr. Paul Gold
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ktwcwpe
materials: Necessary Supplies Bulk affinity resin Di-H 2 O Phosphate Buffer, pH 8 (GoldBio Catalog # P-500) His-Tag Buffer Set (GoldBio Catalog # I-906) Empty plastic column with bottom and top stoppers A beaker or tube to catch flow through A ring stand and clamp Small funnel for head of column

steps.title: Prepare Resin and Buffer
steps.instruction: Completely degas the agarose bead resin and buffer before adding them to the column.

steps.title: Remove Air Bubbles from Column
steps.instruction: Remove air bubbles from under the frit of the empty column using Wash Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add one column volume of Wash Buffer to the empty column.
Slowly drip buffer through the column.
If air bubbles remain, tap the column or centrifuge at a low RPM to remove them.

steps.title: Pack the Column
steps.instruction: Pack the column with Affinity Agarose Beads (Ni, Co, Cu, Zn or Metal Free) to the desired bed height.

substeps.instruction: Gently shake the bead bottle to obtain a homogenous suspension.
Place a funnel in the column head and open the bottom cap to start buffer flow.
Slowly run the bead suspension down the walls of the column.
Continue pouring until the desired bed height is reached, ensuring a continuous pour to prevent beads from settling.
If beads settle, use a pipette to mix the top of the settled matrix before adding more beads.
Ensure the column does not run dry; if it does, the column must be re-poured.
If using a flow adapter, insert it into the column head until it displaces liquid, ensuring no air is trapped under the sintered disc.

steps.title: Wash Preservative from Resin
steps.instruction: Remove the preservative from the resin while ensuring the column does not run dry.

substeps.instruction: Run 5-10 column volumes of Buffer or Di-H2O through the column.

steps.title: Store or Equilibrate Column
steps.instruction: Depending on the timeline, either store the column or proceed to equilibration.

substeps.instruction: For immediate use: Proceed to equilibration.

For storage: Add slightly less than one column volume of Buffer or Di-H2O, place top and bottom caps, and store upright at 4°C. Sodium azide can be added to a final concentration of 0.02% to prevent microbial growth.

steps.title: Equilibrate the Column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the column using degassed Wash Buffer to avoid bubble formation.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 to 10 column volumes of Wash Buffer.

steps.title: Load Lysate
steps.instruction: Load the lysate containing the solubilized 6x Histidine labeled protein onto the column.

substeps.instruction: Control the flow rate; for a 1 ml column, a binding flow rate of 12 ml per hour is recommended.
Alternatively, load one third of the column volume and allow material to bind for five minutes before adding the next load.

steps.title: Wash the Column
steps.instruction: Wash the column with 10 column volumes of Wash Buffer.

substeps.instruction: For a 1 ml column, use a flow rate of 30 ml per hour.
Avoid compressing the Agarose beads by applying excessive pressure via a pump or large pressure head.

steps.title: Elute the Protein
steps.instruction: Elute the protein using either a linear gradient or a step gradient.

substeps.instruction: Method A (Linear Gradient): Apply a linear gradient of 10mM Imidazole to 500mM Imidazole in Phosphate Buffer, pH 8.

Method B (Step Gradient): Use Elution Buffer at 300mM, 400mM, and 500mM Imidazole. Dilute Elution Buffer with Phosphate Buffer, pH 8 as follows: 100mM (50 ml) = 10 ml Elution : 40 ml Phosphate; 200mM (50 ml) = 20 ml Elution : 30 ml Phosphate; 300mM (50 ml) = 30 ml Elution : 20 ml Phosphate; 400mM (50 ml) = 40 ml Elution : 10 ml Phosphate.
Collect fractions commensurate with the column bed volume (e.g., 200 µl fractions for a 1 ml bed column).
Note: Protein should theoretically elute in the included volume, approximately two thirds of the column bed volume.
